The case was filed on August 28 at the Bowbazar police station in Kolkata over a complaint by Shastri Maharaj, described as a Hindu monk. “It raised objection to the term, ‘gerua gundami’ that translates into ‘saffron hooliganism’ that featured in reports by the publication on violent clashes that erupted at Jadavpur University earlier last month,” the statement recalled. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari had attacked the newspaper over the phrase “saffron hooligan” at a media conclave before the complaint was filed. At a rally in Jadavpur, he sought an apology and said thousands of saffron-clad sadhus were ready to act. The paper published the remarks on its front page. After the FIR was filed, the Federation of Press Clubs had last week demanded that the West Bengal government withdraw the case. In a statement on Tuesday, the IWPC and Press Association said, “Journalists work to uncover the truth that can be unpalatable or even offensive to some, but it constitutes the core of our democracy. The increasing incidence of registration of FIRs against journalists is disturbing. It criminalises the journalist and shows disrespect for the role of a free press.” “The complainant asked for a thorough investigation by the police on ‘who proposed the expression, who approved it and who was involved in editing the report and determining the headline and whether any of them had any intention or knowledge that this could cause serious injury to religious sentiment’.” “We know that the language of what is reported and published is decided by the journalist/editors in line with the publication’s norms that fall within the broad contours of ‘parliamentary language. एक मतदाता इस ड्राफ्ट सूची में नहीं है. दिल्ली की 70 विधानसभा सीटों में से सात सीटों पर एक लाख से ज्यादा नाम ड्राफ्ट सूची से बाहर हैं. संख्या के लिहाज से सबसे ज्यादा नाम बुराड़ी, ओखला, बदरपुर, जंगपुरा और बदरपुर में 40% से ज्यादा मतदाता ड्राफ्ट रोल में नहीं हैं. इनमें से तीन सीटें 2025 के दिल्ली विधानसभा चुनाव में आम आदमी पार्टी और दो भारतीय जनता पार्टी (भाजपा) ने जीती थीं. तुगलकाबाद में items.title: Adityanath says UP has 7 months of sugar. Here’s what that calculation misses
items.summary: On August 25, at an event in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath told an audience that there was no sugar crisis in the state. UP consumes about four lakh tonnes of sugar a month. It had about 28 lakh tonnes in stock. Divide the second by the first and you get seven. Seven months of cover. And from October 15, mills would restart and make another 90 lakh tonnes. Reassuring and easy to report. Which is what happened. Now look at what sugar cost that same week. On August 19, Muzaffarnagar mandi hit Rs 5,700 a quintal against Kolhapur’s Rs 5,530. The benchmark mandi of India’s biggest cane state was one of the most expensive places to buy sugar in the country, with UP wholesale up 30.99 percent in three months. So a state supposedly swimming in sugar, but where sugar happened to be among the dearest in the country. Both these facts were reported. They were rarely put next to each other. When you do put them next to each other, you discover something more interesting than a politician being optimistic. You discover that in India, the amount of sugar in a warehouse and the price of sugar in a shop are only loosely related, and that this is not an accident. The number moved Three days before that speech, on August 22, the Chief Minister reportedly held a review meeting . The government said mills in the state were holding 179.38 lakh quintals of sugar. Of this, 23.60 lakh quintals sat with cooperative mills, 5.28 lakh quintals with state corporation mills and 150.50 lakh quintals with private mills. Convert that and you get 17.94 lakh tonnes. Not the 28 he mentioned later. Where do the extra 10 lakh tonnes come from? The likeliest answer is in the same statement, which also noted that mills had sold 235 lakh quintals of sugar in June and July, and that officials believed much of it was still floating around in the open market. But sugar that has already been sold is a different animal from sugar sitting in a mill godown. For two reasons. One, UP mills sell all over India. The state is landlocked, and it sends most of its surplus to deficit regions elsewhere in the country. A good chunk of what left UP mills in June and July also left UP. Two, sold sugar sits with traders. And traders were, that same week, under the scanner. District magistrates had been ordered to physically verify stocks at mills and godowns, and in Meerut division alone the deputy sugarcane commissioner said 2.69 lakh tonnes were under watch . items.summary: All comparisons between deleted names and votes cast in 2025 are size comparisons only, not indications of overlap between the two groups. The draft roll as part of the Special Intensive Revision exercise is out for Delhi. Of 1,45,10,299 electors, 47,56,722 are currently out – nearly one in every three persons excluded. Seven of Delhi’s 70 constituencies recorded more than 1 lakh deletions each. In descending order in terms of sheer numbers, these are Burari, Okhla, Badarpur, Vikaspuri, Matiala, Rithala, and Karawal Nagar. In terms of deletions compared to the size of the electorate, five constituencies had more than 40 percent of their 2025 electorate missing from the draft roll. These were Tughlakabad, Okhla, R.K. items.title: Candidates can claim reservation in Puducherry based on mother's native origin even if father is a migrant: Madras HC
items.summary: The Madras High Court has held that candidates born and raised in Puducherry can claim Scheduled Caste (SC), Most Backward Class (MBC), and Other Backward Class (OBC) reservation benefits based on their mother's native origin status even if their father is a migrant from outside the Union Territory [Thelagam vs Union Territory of Puducherry] By way of an order passed on August 27, Justice D Bharatha Chakravarthy allowed a batch of 28 petitions and set aside orders of the Union Territory administration that had refused or downgraded community certificates to "migrant" status solely because the petitioners' fathers, though of the same caste as their mothers, had moved to Puducherry from other States. The Court rejected Puducherry's position that caste status must be traced through the father since Indian society is patriarchal. The Court ruled that such reasoning cannot be sustained under Articles 14, 15 and 16 of the Constitution, particularly after the 2004 amendment to the Hindu Succession Act gave women equal coparcenary rights. "The society is driven as under by ‘Caste’, and it operates to a great extent in the minds of the people. Similarly, while sex is true, in that any person is born as male, female or intersex, gender stereotypes are based on stories and beliefs built over a period of time, and they are not necessarily true," the Court said in its order. Justice D Bharatha Chakravarthy Madras High Court The society is driven as under by ‘Caste’, and it operates to a great extent in the minds of the people. Applying the Supreme Court's test in Rameshbhai Dabhai Naik vs State of Gujarat, the Court held that by virtue of being the son of a forward caste father he did not have any advantageous start in life but on the contrary suffered the deprivations, indignities, humilities and handicaps like any other member of the community to which his/her mother belonged. Since the petitioners were born, educated and continuously resident in Puducherry within their mothers' communities, they satisfied this test regardless of the father's migrant status, the Court ruled. The Court also disagreed with the Additional Government Pleader's submission that Division Benches of the High Court were split on the issue. It noted that only three Division Bench rulings had gone against recognising origin status through the mother. items.title: Woman returning after maternity leave has right to resume duty without change in role, authority: Delhi HC
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently held that a woman employee of a private company returning from maternity leave is entitled to be reinstated in the same position she held before proceeding on leave [Rakhi Bisht v. Union of India and Anr] . Justice Sachin Datta said that any reassignment causing a change in her responsibilities, authority or status will be presumed discriminatory unless the employer can show compelling, bona fide reasons unconnected to maternity. The Court reasoned that the prohibitions contained in Section 12(1) of the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 and Section 68(1) of the Code on Social Security, 2020 against disadvantaging a woman during protected maternity leave extends beyond termination or reduction in salary. “The expression “conditions of service” extends to the substantive incidents of employment, including the nature and content of the duties entrusted to her, her grade and functional status, reporting hierarchy, supervisory responsibilities, and her entitlement to be considered for appraisal and promotion. Retention of the same designation and remuneration is, therefore, necessary but not by itself sufficient if changes are brought about in respect of the aforesaid attributes, to her detriment.” The Court also directed the Central government to frame rules within 6 months under the Code on Social Security addressing post-maternity reinstatement, lactation support, creche disclosure and grievance redressal timelines, in consultation with State governments and industry bodies. Justice Sachin Datta Justice Datta rendered these findings while dealing with plea filed by Rakhi Bisht, a chartered accountant (CA) with about 14 years of experience. Bisht had approached the Court alleging that her private sector employer sidelined her to a lower, largely clerical role after she returned from maternity leave in July 2024. The employer allegedly stripped her of her reporting team and left her out of managerial meetings even as her male colleagues were promoted to Senior Manager. However, the company contested the maintainability of the writ petition, arguing that the dispute arose from a private contract of employment and fell outside writ jurisdiction of the Court. It denied any demotion, pointing out that Bisht's designation, salary and even an annual increment remained unchanged. items.title: Press release led to mob violence: Gauhati HC pulls up Mizoram Police for revealing key details of murder probe
items.summary: The Gauhati High Court recently pulled up Mizoram authorities over a police press release that disclosed sensitive details of an ongoing criminal investigation and exposed a suspect’s family to public retaliation [C Laltanpuii v The State of Mizoram & Ors.] . By way of an order passed on August 27, Justice Rajesh Mazumdar declared the press release issued by the Mizoram Police on January 27 to be in violation of the prescribed Police Manual for Media Briefing. "The impugned press release is declared to violate the protocol laid down in the Police Manual for media briefing. The authority who had issued the aforesaid press release shall cause the same to be recalled forthwith and in any case, within a period of 7 days from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order," directed the Court. The Court also directed weekly monitoring of the investigation into the mob violence that followed. Justice Rajesh Mazumdar The case concerned the death of a young woman whose body was found near a football playground in December, 2025. During the investigation, police suspected the husband of petitioner, who died three days later after falling from the first floor of his home. In its January press release, the police identified the deceased-husband as the principal accused and disclosed sensitive details from the ongoing investigation, including suspected bloodstains in his vehicle, call-detail records, forensic findings and personal details about the victim, including her pregnancy. The Court held that such disclosures went beyond the limits prescribed under the Police Manual for Media Briefing. It noted that the police had revealed evidence theories, forensic details and investigative tactics while the investigation was still underway. The Court said the disclosure had immediate consequences for the petitioner's family. "This disclosure had admittedly and obviously led to public outrage and mob violence," the judge noted. On the same day as the press release, three local organisations issued notices stating that the petitioner's family would no longer be allowed to reside within the jurisdiction of the concerned local council. An angry mob subsequently gathered at the family's residence, where construction work was underway, and allegedly resorted to stone-pelting, burning and looting. items.title: Kerala consumer court orders Kalyan Silks to pay ₹31,500 for misleading Onam offer
items.summary: The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (DCDRC) at Ernakulam recently directed Kalyan Silks to pay ₹31,500 to a customer after finding that its Onam advertisement promising ₹1,500 in shopping benefits on a purchase of ₹3,000 was misleading and amounted to an unfair trade practice [Venugopala Pillai PV v M/S Kalyan Silks] A Bench of President DB Binu along with members V Ramachandran and Sreevidhia TN observed that although the ₹1,500 benefit was prominently advertised, important conditions for availing the benefit were not displayed with similar prominence. " In consumer advertising, what is given by the headline cannot effectively be taken away by inconspicuous fine print. The principal claim and the material conditions must convey the same commercial proposition, " the commission said on August 21. It thus directed Kalyan Silks to pay ₹1,500 towards the advertised shopping benefit and ₹25,000 as compensation for unfair trade practice, deficiency in service, inconvenience, mental distress, and loss of time. It also awarded ₹5,000 towards litigation costs. The order was passed on a complaint filed by 81-year-old RTI and consumer protection activist, Venugopala Pillai PV. According to the complaint, Kalyan Silks had published a full-page advertisement in Mathrubhoomi newspaper in August 2023 stating that customers purchasing goods worth ₹3,000 would receive shopping benefits worth ₹1,500. Attracted by the offer, Pillai and his family members visited the showroom and selected garments worth ₹4,055. However, he was later informed that the ₹1,500 benefit would be given through three coupons of ₹500 each and that each coupon could be used only against a separate purchase of at least ₹1,500 during September, October and November 2023. The commission noted that this meant that a customer had to make three further purchases totaling at least ₹4,500 to get the entire ₹1,500 benefit which was advertised. It ruled that these were not minor conditions since they substantially changed the nature of the promotional offer. " The difference between an immediate shopping benefit of ₹1,500/- and three future conditional discounts linked to separate minimum purchases is commercially substantial. A prominent claim cannot be evaluated in isolation from conditions that materially alter its meaning, " the commission said. Kalyan Silks argued that the conditions were disclosed in the advertisement and were also explained by its salesman and cashier before the purchase

items.title: Sex with minor wife can attract offence under POCSO Act; Muslim personal law no defence: Kerala High Court
items.summary: The Kerala High Court recently refused to quash a case against a man accused of repeatedly raping a 17-year-old girl, holding that the alleged marital relationship between them could not protect him from prosecution. Justice Jobin Sebastian made the observation in an order dated August 19, 2026, while dismissing a plea by the accused who claimed that the minor victim was his legally wedded wife and that their marriage had been solemnised according to Muslim religious rites. The accused had been charged under Section 375 of the Indian Penal Code as well as the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012. Insofar as the POCSO offences were concerned, the Court said that even if such a marriage had taken place under Muslim personal law, it would not protect the accused from criminal liability since the girl was below the age of 18. " Even assuming for the sake of argument that a marriage was solemnized as per Muslim religious rites and ceremonies, the same will not salvage the petitioner's criminal liability, particularly since the girl was seventeen years old at the time of the alleged marriage and subsequent sexual acts. Undisputedly, the provisions of the POCSO Act apply if one of the parties to the marriage is a minor, irrespective of the validity or otherwise of the marriage under personal law, " the Court stated. Justice Jobin Sebastian The prosecution's case was that the accused had taken the minor girl to his residence on October 23, 2021 and forcefully raped her that night and for the next 4 days. It was alleged that even the accused's parents had facilitated the commission of the crime. Criminal proceedings were initiated against the accused, after which he approached the High Court to quash the proceedings. He claimed that he had married the girl on July 23, 2021 when she was 17 years and 1 month old in accordance with Islamic religious rites and in the presence of members of both families. The Court, however, noted that there was no documentary evidence showing the solemnisation of the marriage. Whether the marriage was valid was to be determined during the trial, it added. It noted that Section 2(1)(d) of the POCSO Act defines 'child' as any person below the age of 18. items.summary: The Delhi High Court has directed the Madhya Pradesh government to pay ₹78.65 lakh as outstanding professional fees to Senior Advocate and the state’s former Advocate General (AG) Anoop George Chaudhari for his appearance before the Supreme Court While the State denied having engaged Chaudhari, the High Court noted that order sheets in the matter proved otherwise. Further, the State's former Chief Secretary had also admitted to having engaged Chaudhari. In view of the same, Justice Sachin Datta said that the fees should be paid to Chaudhari with an interest of 9% per annum from the year 2021, when the petition was filed before the High Court, till the date the final payment is made. In its 55-page order dated August 31, the Court deprecated the conduct of the State of Madhya Pradesh, observing that an advocate’s right to receive payment for services rendered is not merely a legal entitlement but also a matter of honour. Justice Datta underscored that if States are permitted to avail the services of the senior members of the Bar in the hour of need, and then to consign their bills to a maze of departmental denials, the inevitable consequence is that talented members of the Bar will be discouraged from appearing for the State at all. “The dignity of the legal profession, and the effective representation of the State itself before the courts, alike demand that the fees of counsel engaged by the State be paid promptly, and that disputes, where genuinely they exist, be raised contemporaneously and in good faith,” the Court said. items.title: Karnataka HC grants relief to man booked for sexual harassment after urinating near railway track
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Tuesday quashed criminal proceedings filed against a man accused of sexually harassing a woman after she came across him attending nature's call near a railway track. The complainant woman had accused the accused man of exposing his private parts to her and making certain inappropriate gestures at her. The Court, however, found that it appeared to be a case where the accused man had made some gestures out of shock when he found that the woman had seen him while he was urinating. Justice M Nagaprasanna opined that this cannot amount to the offence under Section 75 (2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS), which deals with the offence of sexual harassment. The Court, therefore, allowed the accused man's plea to quash the criminal case against him. " The petitioner admittedly, even according to the complaint, was answering a nature's call ... after searching for a public toilet all over and not finding it ... The gesture that the complainant narrates is only a shock that the petitioner saw the complainant, as is narrated in the statement itself. That would not become in the considered view of this court an ingredient of outraging the modesty of a woman under Section 75(2). Permitting further proceedings at the case at hand on the aforesaid score would on the face of it become an abuse of the process of law and result in miscarriage of justice," it said. Justice M Nagaprasanna The 26-year-old accused man was was travelling on a long-distance bus when the incident took place. He told the Court that he had deboarded his bus to use the restroom. However, after he was unable to find a public toilet, he proceeded to relieve himself near a railway track. A 22-year-old woman was walking by when the accused man turned around. The woman claimed that in doing so, he exposed his private part to her and made gestures at her. She proceeded to file a criminal complaint against him for sexual harassment. Following a police investigation, the accused man was eventually charged for sexual harassment under Section 75 (2) of the BNS. A trial court also took cognisance of the case and summoned him for trial. The accused man proceeded to challenge these criminal proceedings before the High Court. The High Court today allowed his plea and quashed the case against him. Advocate Abhilash HS represented the petitioner (accused man) Advocate Swati Gopalkrishna appeared for the complainant.

A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi , and Justice V Mohana invoked Article 142 of the Constitution to quash the criminal cases after the Central government and respective governments moved applications to seek quashing of the cases. The Court also directed that similar FIRs in other States and Union Territories – other than Delhi, Bihar, Maharashtra, West Bengal and Assam - shall not be pursued or investigated, meaning they shall be considered closed for all intents and purposes. It further ordered that compensation be paid within three months to the families of students who committed suicide in connection with NEET 2026 after formulation of a pan-India policy, in accordance with the assurances made by Central government to the CJP leadership. The top court has been hearing a batch of petitions related to CJP protests, including the use of excessive force against protestors in Delhi and Bihar. In an application filed in the matter on Monday, the Central government urged the Supreme Court to quash 13 FIRs registered between July 20 and 25 by Delhi Police. However, the Union government also said that it will continue prosecution against 2,873 individuals in Delhi with "serious criminal antecedents" as per the National Crime Records Bureau database. items.title: RGNUL faculty say dispute with Vice-Chancellor remains unresolved 3 weeks on; launch 'no cooperation' campaign
items.summary: About 3 weeks into their dispute with the administration, faculty members of Rajiv Gandhi National University of Law (RGNUL), Patiala say nothing has changed. The dispute began on August 10, when RGNUL faculty gave the University a 48-hour notice . They alleged misconduct by Vice-Chancellor (VC) Prof (Dr) Jai S Singh and sought the Chancellor's intervention. Faculty had alleged irregularities in promotions, interference in the curriculum, an opaque functioning of the VC's office and questionable appointments that bypassed the Registrar and Deans. Non-teaching staff followed with their own 48-hour notice the next day, over unresolved promotions and other service grievances. On August 12, the Vice-Chancellor issued a notice directing an end to the strike and withdrew the disputed promotion at the centre of the faculty's complaint. But faculty said at the time that he had taken no real steps to resolve the underlying issues and that a pen-down strike went ahead regardless. On August 27, the faculty wrote to the VC again asking what he was doing to resolve the situation. He gave no clear answer, they said. He then called a meeting on August 31. According to faculty, his only agenda item was to organise a guest lecture and call it a "National Conference", to which all faculty objected. At the same meeting, the faculty said, the VC stated that he was not interested in a second term at RGNUL and planned to join his parent institution to claim his retirement benefits. With no real agenda set, the faculty said that they raised their concerns directly. The VC then had the meeting's proceedings formally recorded, a first according to faculty. However, he then allegedly had photographs of the meeting taken despite objections by the faculty. Faculty members claim that the VC routinely circulates such material over WhatsApp within his circle. They feared he could also send the photographs to higher University authorities to project that he was in control of the situation and that faculty had been calmed down. The teachers also said that the VC spent much of the meeting on a discussion about changing the nature of certain University offices. This, they said, was aimed at placing "cronies" in important posts to protect his own position. The meeting ignored their priority concerns, they said. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday declined to entertain Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra's petition seeking directions to appear virtually before police in a case accusing her of uploading a provocative post on Facebook A Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu brushed off Moitra's concerns that eggs may be pelted on her in case she goes to the police station. "You are a member of parliament? Having taken the plunge into politics, you fear eggs? When our freedom fighters have taken bullets on their chest? items.title: Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar’s promise: Will the state fulfil the dreams of our youth?
items.summary: It is heartening to note that Karnataka’s CM DK Shivakumar has recognised that “the power, dreams, thinking, and hard work of our youth are the divine forces that determine India’s future.” He recently went on to promise that safeguarding the ideas, aspirations, and rights of youth “must be the foremost priority of any responsible government”. This is indeed a reassuring statement for our youth. But there may be a long way to go before every single youth of the state becomes “a bright shining lamp, or ‘Siri Hanate’, illuminating the state’s future”, as the CM wishes. In a hard-hitting article in Praja Pragathi , Dr MG Priyanka, an Assistant Professor in Tumakuru University, has recounted how “the futures of thousands of children are perishing every morning right before our eyes in Karnataka”. She cites instances of the following cruel paradox: “Where 14-year-old children should be wearing a school bag on their backs, the crushing weight of hunger has forced them to carry iron rods, loads of bricks, and grease-stained garage tools!” She narrates examples of a 15-year-old girl in Bagalkot’s brick kilns, stacking hot bricks at 2 am and weeping, "I want to go to school, Sir"; and how a 14-year-old boy’s grease-dipped fingers were crushed in the gears of the lathe machine that he was working on. The harsh reason for this state of affairs among our teenagers exposed by the Union Ministry of Education’s UDISE+ report is that Karnataka bears the shame of ranking first in the entire country for high school dropouts (Grades 9 and 10), recording a shocking overall dropout rate of 18.1%, and the even more shocking rate of 22% for boys. In contrast, the national average is half our figure at 9.5%. During the transition from high school to the Pre-University Course (PUC) level, the net enrollment rate in the state sinks drastically to 62.4%. But are our schools fit enough to retain the drop-outs? Dr Priyanka again gives the revealing statistics of how in the border regions of Yadgir and Raichur, 60 to 70 9th-grade students sit all day staring at empty blackboards because there are no permanent teachers for mathematics and science. Teacher shortages in Kalyan Karnataka stand at 35.8%. In Pavagada, a 14-year-old girl stopped drinking water all day because there was no toilet at school and ended up hospitalised with a severe urinary tract infection. items.title: Hyderabad: Art director Anand Sai’s son arrested in hit-and-run after man dies
items.summary: The Cyberabad police on Tuesday, September 1, arrested Sandeep, son of prominent art director Anand Sai, in connection with a hit-and-run case under the Raidurgam police limits. Anand Sai is reportedly a close associate of Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan. He is also known for designing the Yadadri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple and is a member of the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) Board. According to reports, Sandeep allegedly ran over a man identified as Nandulal near the main road connecting the Outer Ring Road (ORR) and Khajaguda before fleeing the spot. As Nandulal was being rescued by a student, identified as Zaid Shah Qadri, another speeding car allegedly hit him, leaving him seriously injured. Nandulal later died. Police subsequently traced Sandeep using CCTV footage and identified the vehicles involved in the accident. “Sandeep has been detained for questioning; we cannot reveal details of the accident right now,” a police officer was quoted as saying by Siasat. The arrest comes days after another high-profile road accident in Hyderabad involving the son of a Jana Sena Party leader. On August 16, 26-year-old Bharati Mukhi, an employee at Inorbit Mall, was killed after being hit by an Aston Martin near the mall. Police identified the driver as 21-year-old Lingamaneni Sanjush, son of Andhra Pradesh Rajya Sabha MP and Jana Sena leader Lingamaneni Ramesh.

items.title: KRV and MNS meet in Bengaluru to build national language equality movement
items.summary: The larger goal behind the recent meeting of Kannada and Marathi language groups in Bengaluru was to build a language equality movement, foster federalism, and advocate for the rights of states, Karnataka Rakshana Vedike (KRV) leader Arun Javgal said, while acknowledging that there are tensions between the two groups. KRV’s meeting with members of the Maharashtra Navanirman Sena (MNS) had taken many by surprise and sparked interest on social media, as both groups have previously clashed over language-related issues along the Karnataka-Maharashtra border. Arun Javgal and others of KRV met with Maharashtra Navanirman Sena general secretary Yogesh Parolekar and Mumbai president Sandeep Deshpande on August 29 and 30 in Bengaluru. Calling it a “long-pending meeting”, Arun said , “For more than two decades, both KRV and MNS have been fighting against Hindi imposition and for the linguistic and employment rights of our respective people.” He added that “mutual support and understanding between the two organisations is not new” and that the two organisations have supported each other’s campaigns in the past. Maintaining that KRV was committed to Kannada interests, Arun said that the two groups must fight for common issues. “The fight against Hindi imposition is not a Karnataka-versus-Maharashtra issue. It concerns linguistic equality, the rights of all Indian languages, and a genuinely federal India,” he said. Language equality Speaking to TNM, Arun pointed out that the idea for the meeting did not come out of the blue, nor was it the first time that KRV has collaborated with language rights groups. He said that a round table conference was held in 2017, involving language rights groups from West Bengal, Punjab, Tamil Nadu, and other states. For several years, he said, MNS and KRV supported each others’ campaigns, although it was mostly online. The idea now, Arun said, was to build a national-level forum to fight for language equality. “There are issues, such as the Cauvery river water dispute and the border issue with Maharashtra. But despite the problems, we can fight along with other language groups for common issues. ” He said that the two-day meeting involved discussions on setting up a national level forum, holding events in different cities, and initiating discussions with other language groups. “We want to invite even Hindi groups to talk about language quality. items.title: Chennai woman dies by suicide allegedly over dowry harassment
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. A 27-year-old woman identified as Bhuvaneswari, died by suicide at her parents’ house in Chennai, allegedly after facing continuous harassment from her husband’s family over dowry. The victim had completed three degrees and previously worked as a teacher. Bhuvaneswari’s mother told the media that her daughter had been facing harassment from her husband Janakiraman’s family, who allegedly demanded additional dowry. Bhuvaneswari married Janakiraman on September 8, 2024. Her family had given her 50 sovereigns of gold and her husband 20 sovereigns as dowry. On August 16, the couple celebrated their son’s first birthday. According to Bhuvaneswari’s family, Janakiraman’s family demanded an additional 20 sovereigns of gold for the occasion. Her family, however, gave two sovereigns, following which an argument allegedly broke out. Last Thursday, Janakiraman dropped Bhuvaneswari at her parents’ house for a temple festival. He later called her on Saturday and allegedly told her to remain at her parents’ house. While her family had gone to the temple for the festival, Bhuvaneswari allegedly attempted suicide. She was rushed to Tambaram Government Hospital, where she died. Her family subsequently informed the Pallikaranai police about the incident. Further investigation is underway. items.title: Chennai: Man arrested for stabbing bedridden father to death
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. A 45-year-old man, Natarajan, has been arrested for stabbing his father, Rajendran, who had been bedridden for a month due to a leg injury. The incident happened on August 30 near Thiru Vi Ka nagar, Chennai. Though Rajendran was rushed to a hospital, he was declared dead. Three days before the incident, Natarajan’s wife, Ezhila Mary, had gone to Velankanni with their two children. Before leaving, she had asked Natarajan to take care of his father. When Ezhila returned home on Sunday morning, she found the house unclean and noticed that Rajendran had soiled the bed as he was unable to move around. She scolded Natarajan for failing to take proper care of his father. Police told TNM that an argument broke out between Natarajan and Rajendran. As the argument escalated, Natarajan allegedly stabbed his father with a knife. The police have registered a case under Section 103(1) — Punishment for Murder — of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, and arrested Natarajan. items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has claimed that India’s GDP grew by 7.8% in the April-June quarter of 2026-27, calling it a reflection of the “collective strength” and hard work of Indians. But alongside celebrating the growth, Modi also renewed his appeal to citizens to avoid foreign holidays, weddings abroad and unnecessary gold purchases. In a video message posted on Tuesday, September 1, Modi said India had achieved the growth despite wars, global instability and disruptions to supply chains. He also accused some people in India of spreading negativity and “jhooth ki goonj” — an apparent reference to Congress leader Rahul Gandhi. So, what exactly did Modi say, and why did he bring up foreign travel, weddings and gold while talking about GDP growth? What did Modi say about the 7.8% growth? According to the PM, India’s real GDP grew by 7.8% in the April-June quarter, the first quarter of the 2026-27 financial year. The growth was higher than the 6.9% recorded in the same quarter last year, though lower than the 8.6% growth recorded in January-March 2026. Modi congratulated Indians on the growth, saying it was the result of their “resolve and industrious spirit”. He also pointed to the global situation, saying India had continued to progress despite wars, instability and supply-chain disruptions. “Since the 2020 COVID pandemic, there has been no stability anywhere, but India has progressed well,” he said. He said India now needed to maintain the momentum and become more self-reliant, or Atmanirbhar. Why did he talk about ‘Swadeshi’? Modi linked the GDP numbers to his long-standing push for Swadeshi and “Vocal for Local”, encouraging people to buy Indian-made products and spend more within the domestic economy. His argument was that greater reliance on Indian products and services would strengthen the domestic economy and contribute to making India self-reliant. “The more we emphasise Swadeshi, the more we emphasise self-reliance,” Modi said, adding that this would help India present a developed country to its young people when India reaches 100 years of Independence. Why did he ask people not to travel abroad? Modi specifically asked people to avoid foreign travel when it is only for leisure. items.title: In India, abortion remains stigmatised, even though legally permitted
items.summary: “Life begins at conception,” Tamil Nadu Assembly Speaker JCD Prabhakar said at a recent anti-abortion event in Chennai. This triggered questions around abortion rights, access, legality, reproductive autonomy, and the role of the State, all of which require a considered and evidence-based response . This moment warrants an effort to understand how abortion is perceived in a country where reproductive autonomy has been under Article 21 (Protection of life and personal liberty) and where abortion, though broadly criminalised under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, is legally permitted within the framework of the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act. At the same time, it also offers an opportunity to reflect on the narratives shaping abortion discourse in India, who gets to define them, and whose experiences are heard. While individuals are entitled to personal religious beliefs, can a constitutional authority invoke theological doctrine to undermine women's legally and constitutionally protected rights? Does the MTP Act ensure access to abortion care? India has one of the more progressive legal frameworks on abortion globally. Successive amendments to the MTP Act have expanded the circumstances under which abortion can be accessed, increased gestational limits, and strengthened legal protections around confidentiality. Yet on the ground, this legally permissive framework doesn’t always translate to accessible services for comprehensive abortion care, more so for adolescents and people marginalised by their identities and geographical barriers. The law still does not recognise abortion “on request”, access continues to be mediated through statutory conditions, gestational limits, and required permission from registered medical practitioners and authorised facilities; the addition of medical boards in the 2021 MTP (Amendment) Act has furthered third party authorisation. In practice, abortion seekers continue to struggle with multiple intersecting barriers such as finding a trained provider, an authorised facility, affordable care, or timely services. Provider discretion, pervasive stigma, lack of information, geographical distances, and fear of disclosure further shape whether and when care can be accessed. The legal framework also leaves important gaps. The Act remains deeply cis-normative, using gendered language such as “pregnant woman” and failing to recognise the needs of LGBTQIA+ people who can become pregnant.
